issues.failure_explanation: By eq:Mp, M_d acts on the last tensor factor through -(\vrho{L,d}{})^T, so a product u^{l_1,d}_{j_1}⊗...⊗u^{L,d}_j is an eigenvector of M_d only if u^{L,d}_j is an eigenvector of the transpose (\vrho{L,d}{})^T, not of \vrho{L,d}{} as the proposition states; for non-normal \vrho{L,d}{} these differ. Concrete counterexample: N=1, \vrho{l_1,d}{}=[1], \vrho{L,d}{}=A=[[1,1],[0,2]]; then M_d=I-A^T has kernel span{(1,-1)^T} (the eigenvector of A^T for eigenvalue 1), while the proposition predicts span{(1,0)^T} (the eigenvector of A for eigenvalue 1), which is not in the kernel. Additionally, the claim that the products span ker(M_d) presupposes a complete set of |\calM_l| eigenpairs, i.e. diagonalizability of each \vrho{l,d}{}, which fails for nilpotent generators of general linear Lie group representations (e.g. M_d=N⊗I+I⊗N with N a 2x2 Jordan block has a 2-dimensional kernel while only one product eigenvector exists). (Note eq:Mp itself is the transpose of the matrix defined by eq:M_GE, consistent with the same sign/transpose mishandling.)

issues.failure_explanation: For L<\sum\bl the matrix M_2^- is block upper-bidiagonal with invertible diagonal blocks A^-_K and one extra bottom block row [B^-_{-L},0,...]. Invertibility of the A^-_K plus full row rank of the single corner block B^-_{-L} does not imply full row rank of M_2^-: eliminating the invertible diagonal blocks propagates the bottom row to a Schur-type complement B^-_{-L}(A^-_{-L})^{-1}B^-_{-L+1}...(A^-_{L-1})^{-1}B^-_L whose rank must equal |\calM_{\bl,-L-1}|. Equivalently, a row-dependency analysis requires controlling the left null spaces and row spaces of all intermediate blocks B^-_K (K=-L+1,...,L), which are rectangular with nontrivial left kernels; the established identities (eq:Bequality, eq:ladder2) give the needed positive-definiteness only at the corners K=\pm(L+1). The same gap recurs in the proof that M^up has full rank and, in weighted form, in the GE-PI analog prop:ker-M2-GEPI. The conclusions are correct (they reproduce the classical tensor-product multiplicity |\calM_{\bl,L}|-|\calM_{\bl,L+1}|), but as written the full-rank claims, the equality ker(M^up)=ker(M_2), and the resulting dimension formulas rest on an unproven step.

issues.title: Full-rank proof for the block-bidiagonal matrices M_2^- and M^up has a missing nontrivial argument
issues.why_classification: The statements are correct and a contained nontrivial argument (a new lemma on the ladder blocks, or citing the standard sl_2 weight-space facts) repairs the proofs without changing any conclusion; no result is abandoned and no global restructuring is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For N=1 the formula sums terms \binom{\cdot}{-1}, which is 0 under the combinatorial convention (\binom{n}{k}=0 for n<k) that the inclusion-exclusion counting formula for |\calM_{\bl,L}| itself requires; the formula then evaluates to 0, whereas the true value is \dimge{(l)}{L}=\delta_{L,l} (e.g. bl=(l), L=l gives 1 by eq:dim_su2, since |\calM_{\bl,l}|-|\calM_{\bl,l+1}|=1-0). The derivation's Pascal-identity step is applied with k=N-2=-1, where \binom{n}{-1}+\binom{n}{0}=\binom{n+1}{0} fails at the boundary n=-1 under that convention. Hence the proposition is valid only for N\ge 2 as derived.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the proposition to N\ge 2 and note the trivial N=1 case \dimge{(l)}{L}=\delta_{L,l} (or adopt a convention/boundary handling that keeps the Pascal step valid at k=-1).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit dimension formula (eq:explicit_dim_GE) is wrong in the degenerate case N=1; for N\ge 2 it is correct, and all uses in the paper (Example exam:dim_cg_su2 with N=2, tables computed otherwise) are unaffected.
issues.title: Explicit GE dimension formula fails at N=1
issues.why_classification: Fixing a degenerate case by adding the standard restriction N\ge 2 preserves the method, conclusions and advertised scope; the N=1 content is trivially recovered.

issues.failure_explanation: The two supporting estimates used in the proof hold only for bounded L: in general H_4(x_L)-H_4(x_{L+1})=O(L/N) (since H_4'(x)=O(x) near 0 and \Delta x=1/\sqrt{Var}), and the exponential difference equals \frac{2L+1}{2Var}e^{-L^2/2Var}+O(L^3/N^2), not \frac{2L+1}{2Var}+O(N^{-2}). With L allowed to grow within the stated regime L\ll\sqrt{Var} (e.g. L\asymp N^{1/4}), the dropped exponential factor changes the leading term by a relative O(L^2/N), giving an absolute error of order L N^{-5/2}\asymp N^{-9/4}, which violates the claimed uniform O(N^{-5/2}). The proof therefore establishes (eq:dimge-est) only for bounded L. The same defect propagates to Proposition prop:asym-dim-gepi, whose proof is declared 'similar' and which states the same O(\Nb^{-5/2}) error over L\ll\sqrt{Var}.
